about_text:
TopoTrail

Version {version}

A tool supporting the planning of trails, access routes and field movement in natural and protected areas. From a single digital elevation model it produces the terrain suitability map, the potential access zones, the least-cost route with its walking time, and the watercourses the route crosses.

Development: Luan da Silva Cortes Maciel (MACIEL, L. S. C.)
Supervision: Leandro Freitas
Associated project: Herpeto Mantiqueira

Context: developed as a product of master's research in Biodiversity in Protected Areas, Escola Nacional de Botânica Tropical / Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden Research Institute.

How to cite: Maciel, L. S. C. (2026). TopoTrail: a QGIS plugin for DEM-based topographic suitability and least-cost route planning (version {version}) [Computer software]. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/{doi}

Results are decision-support evidence and require field validation.

User guide · Source code · Report a problem
MIT licence
report_intro: Something went wrong, or a text was confusing? Tell us what happened. The technical details below go along and help find the cause; check them before sending.
report_placeholder: What you did, what you expected and what happened.
report_attach:
If you can, attach the technical log of this run to the e-mail:
{path}
report_github_tip: For GitHub users: the report is public and you can follow the fix.
report_note: The e-mail goes to {email}. It opens in your e-mail program with the text ready; if you use webmail, click Copy text and paste it into a message.
report_sent: Your e-mail program should open with the message ready. The text was also copied: if nothing opens, paste it into a message to {email}.
report_no_mail: No e-mail program opened. The text has been copied: paste it into a message to {email}.
report_copied: Text copied. Paste it into a message to {email}.
report_github_done: The form opened in your browser, already filled in. Sending it requires signing in to a GitHub account.
alg_basin: Minimum contributing area to count as a channel (km²)
alg_breaks: Slope breaks for the transitability classes (%)
alg_derive: Derive slope and curvatures from the DEM itself
alg_extradir: In the additional criterion, high values are
alg_help: Generates potential trail zones by boolean constraints and a weighted linear combination of DEM-derived terrain criteria, with a least-cost route (Tobler walking time) and an access corridor.
alg_lim_curvh: Plan curvature normalisation limit (0 = scene P99)
alg_lim_curvv: Profile curvature normalisation limit (0 = scene P99)
alg_lim_rough: VRM ruggedness normalisation limit (0 = scene P95)
alg_cell: Working cell size in metres (0 = automatic; fix it to compare clips)
alg_field_speed: Field survey speed (km/h), for the field time estimate
alg_optimise: Choose the best visiting order (ignores layer order)
alg_slopescore: Slope at which the score reaches zero (%)
alg_streams: Take watercourses extracted from the DEM into account
alg_walkzones: Generate zones as a continuous walkable area
breaks_help: Four increasing values separating the five classes.
chip_unreadable: I could not open this file as a raster
cons_help: Features to keep away from: a fence, a closed area, private land, an exclusion zone. Anything that constrains movement where you work — the layer is yours.
coord_help: X, Y coordinates in the project CRS (the map's CRS). Or pick on the map.
cost: How to measure the cost of the path
cost_help: Tobler: uphill costs more than downhill and the cost comes out in hours. Validated against field GPS.
credit_line: ENBT · Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden · Herpeto Mantiqueira
crs_help: Left blank, the project CRS is used.
dem_help: An elevation raster in GeoTIFF. Any source works: Copernicus, SRTM, ALOS, a national topographic sheet.
developed_by: Developed by MACIEL, L. S. C.
route_missing_text:
{count} layer(s) loaded — zones and maps — but the route was not produced:

{error}
err_alt: Minimum altitude must be lower than maximum.
err_breaks: Transitability breaks must be four increasing numbers, separated by commas.
err_dem: Choose the digital elevation model to continue.
err_dem_invalid:
I could not open this raster as a valid layer:
{path}
err_not_registered: The algorithm topotrail:topotrail is not registered in QGIS. Restart QGIS or re-enable the plugin.
err_out: Choose where to save the result.
err_points: A route needs both an origin and a destination.
err_rasters: You ticked that you will use your own rasters, so slope and both curvatures are required.
err_weights: At least one weight must be greater than zero.
extra_help: Any raster of yours can enter the model: stoniness, vegetation cover, a ready-made cost surface.
ford_max_help: Watercourses whose basin is larger than this are treated as barriers: the route does not cross them. Smaller ones are crossed, and each crossing goes to its own file, classed by size (< 2 km² headwater stream, 2–10 km² stream, above that small river).
ford_river_small: small river — fording depends on the season
group_always_sub: Baseline results for reading the terrain
log_empty: Messages from the computation appear here while it runs.
margin_help: How far the route may stray from the straight line. Too small forces a straight route; too large is slow.
alternatives_help: Shows every path up to this much more costly than the route. If it splits into two valleys, the model does not pin the route down. 0 turns it off.
min_area_help: Automatic: 0.05% of the analysed area, from 1 to 50 ha. Type a value to fix it; 0 turns the filter off.
note_tuning: Conservative defaults — report the ones you use
o_risk_help: Slope and curvature combined at 0.75 and 0.25, to read directly where the terrain is least favourable. It is not the inverse of suitability.
o_route: Route between points, and access corridor
o_route_help: Least-cost path from origin to destination, calling wherever you want on the way.
o_route_tip: Use intermediate destinations to chain objectives: climb one summit, then another, call at a sampling point, then descend.
o_score_help: A 0-to-1 score per cell, combining the criteria from step 3.
o_streams: Take watercourses into account, extracted from the DEM
o_streams_help: Derives drainage from the relief. The route is not pushed away from watercourses: every crossing is listed with the size of the stream, to check in the field. Zones keep the stream margins, often a sampling target.
o_streams_tip: No hydrography layer needed. Careful in seasonally dry landscapes: a dry bed is often the best walking surface, and in biological survey work drainage is a sampling target — avoiding it can push the route away from what you want to visit.
o_transit_help: Five slope classes, with the legend written into the file.
o_transit_tip:
The labels describe steepness, not a verdict on the walker: on real walked trails, field teams routinely cross classes 4 and 5.

The class distribution depends strongly on DEM resolution — quote the cell size beside any number taken from this map.
o_zones_help: The best areas as polygons, for clipping and area measurement.
optimise: Let the plugin choose the best visiting order
optimise_help: Exact cheapest order, up to eight points.
own_help: Tick only if you prefer your own rasters. Leaving it unticked is recommended: deriving from the DEM removes unit, sign-convention and grid-alignment problems.
own_rasters: I already have slope and curvature rasters and want to use them
percentile_help: 75 keeps the best quarter of the area. Lower is more permissive.
pick_prompt: Click on the map to set: {label}.
s1_banner: Only the DEM is required. Slope and curvatures are derived from it, which removes unit, sign-convention and grid-alignment problems in one step.
s1_sub: Choose the elevation model. TopoTrail handles the derived layers and the grid alignment.
s2_sub: Choose what to generate. The two essential maps are already included.
s3_sub: The defaults are conservative starting points. Tune them to your terrain and report the values you use.
s4_sub: The computation runs in the background; QGIS stays usable.
slope_max_help: Above this a cell counts as unusable. 100% is 45 degrees. The default, 85%, connects the walking trails tested and refuses cable or via ferrata sections; raise it only for a route of that kind.
slope_score: Slope at which the score reaches zero (%)
slope_score_help: Where the slope score reaches zero. If most of your area exceeds this, the criterion stops telling one hillside from another and the plugin warns you.
summary: Summary of what will be produced
translation_draft: Draft translation, not yet reviewed by a native speaker. Corrections are welcome in the repository.
via_help: A point layer: feature order is the order of the traverse. Without it the algorithm skirts the high ground — rightly, since a summit is the expensive place.
vunit_help: Metres for nearly every product. Feet appear in some United States datasets.
w_help: How much each criterion counts towards the final score. Zero switches it off. Altitude is zero on purpose: altitude bands discard good terrain in mountainous regions.
msg_raster_sem_crs_estrito: The input raster has no CRS defined. For scientific use, set the correct CRS at the data source before processing.
msg_dem_sem_crs: DEM without a CRS. CRS assumed for diagnosis: {crs}. The result depends on this assumption; set the correct CRS for scientific use.
msg_latitude_84: The DEM lies above 84 degrees of latitude, outside the UTM domain; the distortion of the chosen zone may be large. Prefer a polar CRS.
msg_crs_nao_metrico: The DEM's CRS ({crs}) does not measure in metres: {reason}. DEM reprojected to the metric working CRS {working}.
msg_grade_reamostrada: DEM with {kind} ({px:.3g} x {py:.3g}); resampled to square {side:.3g} m pixels, north up.
msg_dem_reprojetado: DEM reprojected to the metric working CRS: {crs}.
msg_crs_invalido: The DEM's CRS is neither geographic nor projected. Set a valid CRS before processing.
msg_crs_mantido_celula: DEM kept in the projected CRS {crs}, in aligned {cell:g} m cells.
msg_crs_mantido: DEM kept in its projected CRS: {crs}.
msg_celula_fixa: Fixed working cell of {cell:g} m, aligned to its multiples: different clips of the same area fall on the same grid.
msg_etapa_reprojecao_metrica: DEM reprojection to a metric CRS
msg_etapa_grade_regular: DEM resampling to a regular grid

msg_warp_nao_abre: Error in {step}: the output file does not open: {path}
msg_raster_metadados: Could not open the raster to read its metadata: {path}
msg_raster_sem_crs_abrir: Could not open the raster without a CRS: {path}
msg_raster_copia_crs: Could not create the copy with the CRS set: {path}
msg_gdal_sem_memoria: The GDAL in this installation has no in-memory vector driver.
msg_featureset_sem_crs: Feature set without a source CRS; it cannot be reprojected.
msg_reprojetar_geometria: Failed to reproject the geometry with OSR.
msg_criar_vetor: Could not create the vector file: {path}
msg_criar_camada: Could not create the layer in: {path}
msg_alinhando: Aligning the raster to the DEM: {name}
msg_alinhado_incompativel: The aligned raster is still incompatible with the DEM: {problems}
msg_compat_linhas: different number of rows: reference={reference}, candidate={candidate}
msg_compat_colunas: different number of columns: reference={reference}, candidate={candidate}
msg_compat_geotransform: different GeoTransform at index {index}: reference={reference}, candidate={candidate}
msg_compat_extensao: different extent at index {index}: reference={reference}, candidate={candidate}
msg_raster_banda: Could not read band 1 of the raster: {path}
msg_dimensoes: {name} has dimensions {shape}, but the DEM has {reference}. Resample and align the rasters before processing.
msg_desalinhado: {name} is not aligned with the DEM. Use the same extent, resolution and grid origin for all rasters.
msg_graus_invalido: Slope was declared in degrees, but the raster reaches {maximum:.1f}. Slope in degrees never exceeds 90: this raster is in percent. Correct the unit in the parameter.
msg_graus_convertido: Slope converted from degrees to percent: input max={maximum:.1f} degrees, output max={output:.1f}%.
msg_restricao_sem_crs: The constraint layer has no CRS defined. Set its CRS at the data source before using it as a constraint.
msg_restricao_abrir: Could not open the constraint layer: {source}
msg_restricao_reprojetar: Could not reproject the constraint layer to the working CRS: {error}
msg_restricao_vazia: The constraint layer is empty or has no valid geometries; it was ignored.
msg_restricao_resumo: Constraint layer: {features} features, buffer of {buffer:.0f} m, {cells:,} cells affected ({pct:.2f}% of the grid).
msg_restricao_sem_efeito: The constraint layer did not reach any cell: it had no effect on the route or on the map. A cell is marked only when its centre falls inside a feature, and with a buffer of {buffer:.0f} m no feature covers a cell centre, typically because the feature is narrower than the {pixel:.0f} m pixel. Increase the distance to keep (buffer) to at least {suggested:.0f} m, or use a DEM with smaller cells.
msg_restricoes: Constraints: {cells:,} cells affected ({pct:.2f}% of the valid area), {treatment}.
msg_tratamento_evitar: layer excluded from the zones and the route; drainage only reported on the route (a barrier above the fordable ceiling) and kept in the zones
msg_tratamento_encarecer: layer made {factor:.0f}x costlier; drainage only reported on the route
msg_gpkg_camadas: The output GeoPackage already has {n} layer(s) ({layers}). The layer "{layer}" will be written beside them; nothing already in the file is deleted.
msg_gpkg_bloqueado: The GeoPackage {name} exists and cannot be opened for writing (in use in QGIS or locked by the system). Saving as {alternative} so that the existing file is not lost.
msg_declividade_saturada: {pct:.0f}% of the terrain is above the slope of maximum cost ({score_max:.0f}%), so the slope criterion scores zero over most of the area and no longer tells one hillside from another. In this scene slope has a median of {median:.0f}% and a P90 of {p90:.0f}%. For this relief, consider a slope of maximum cost near {suggested_score:.0f}% and an absolute limit near {suggested_max:.0f}%.
msg_modelo_nao_distingue: Suitability varies by only {amplitude:.3f} between P05 and P95: the model is not distinguishing terrain in this scene, and the resulting zones mean nothing. Review the elevation and slope limits before using this result.
msg_invertido: {name} inverted as cost: min={min:.4f}, max={max:.4f}, mean={mean:.4f}
msg_valores_absurdos: {name}: {cells:,} cells ({pct:.2f}% of the raster) hold values outside any physical scale{extreme}. This is almost always a NoData sentinel value that the file does not declare (-3.4e38, -9999, 1e30). Until it is declared, the criterion is computed with those cells included: the percentile limit blows up, every valid cell scores close to 1 and this criterion stops counting in the model. Declare NoData at the data source or clip to the valid area.
msg_limite_percentil_absurdo: {name}: the percentile limit came out at {limit:.3g}, outside any scale of terrain curvature. With such a limit every valid cell scores close to 1 and the criterion vanishes from the model. Check the NoData of the {name} raster.
msg_resolucao_declividade: Invalid spatial resolution for computing slope.
msg_declividade_calculada: Slope computed at a resolution of {px:.3f} x {py:.3f}: {stats}
msg_resolucao_curvatura: Invalid spatial resolution for computing curvature.
msg_curvaturas_calculadas: Curvatures computed at a resolution of {px:.3f} x {py:.3f}: H={h}, V={v}
msg_mascara_caminhavel: Walkable mask: {valid:,} suitable pixels out of {total:,} ({pct:.2f}%)
msg_limiar_faixas: Threshold by elevation band: {n} bands of {size:.0f} m, percentile {percentile:.1f}
msg_area_minima_filtro: Minimum area filter: {area:.2f} ha, {pixels:,} pixels per patch; {removed:,} patches removed (8 neighbours)
msg_pixels_apos_filtro: Suitable pixels after the filter: {after:,} of {before:,}
msg_area_minima_auto: Automatic minimum patch area: {area:.1f} ha (0.05% of {analysed:,.0f} ha analysed, between 1 and 50 ha).
msg_sem_area_limiar: No area reached the configured threshold. Lower the threshold or review the criteria.
msg_zonas_faixa_auto: Vector zones will use the automatic threshold by elevation band.
msg_zonas_desativadas: Vector zone generation turned off; the raster, the route and the corridor were kept.
msg_nenhuma_zona: No potential zone reached the configured threshold; the raster and the route were kept.
msg_areas_metricas: Could not compute the areas in a metric CRS: {error}
msg_zonas_sem_celulas: No cell meets the constraints of the potential zones, so the zones were not generated; the rasters and the route go ahead. {cause}
msg_repr_frase: Representativeness of the zones in the relief of the analysed area: the zones are present in {parts}.
msg_repr_caminhaveis: Walkable zones follow transitability only and are not chosen by elevation band: if sampling must cover the gradient, generate the zones by suitability with "{option}".
msg_repr_limiar: Elevation bands are on, but they apply only with the automatic threshold: leave the threshold at 0 so that the zones are chosen within each band.
msg_repr_mesmo_com_faixas: Even with elevation bands, part of the gradient is left out: if sampling must represent it, reduce the minimum patch area or the zone percentile.
msg_repr_ligue: The zones do not cover the elevation gradient: if sampling must represent it, turn on "{option}" (step 3: the zones are then chosen within each band).
msg_repr_relevo: The plugin compares relief only. Easy-access zones often coincide with altered land: check land cover (for example, MapBiomas) before choosing the sampling points.
msg_adequabilidade_falhou: Could not create the suitability raster.
msg_adequabilidade_bloqueado: The previous suitability raster is in use in QGIS or locked by the system. Saving the new file as: {path}
msg_transitabilidade_falhou: Could not create the transitability raster.
msg_risco_falhou: Could not create the topographic risk raster.
msg_risco_bloqueado: The previous topographic risk raster is in use in QGIS or locked by the system. Saving the new file as: {path}
msg_risco_resumo: Relative topographic risk: min={min:.3f}, p50={p50:.3f}, p75={p75:.3f}, p95={p95:.3f}, max={max:.3f}
msg_raster_temporario: Could not create the temporary raster.
msg_vetor_temporario: Could not create the temporary vector.
msg_kml_4326: KML is written in EPSG:4326 by definition of the format; the requested output CRS does not apply.
msg_shapefile_area: Field area_m2 removed from the Shapefile output so as not to overflow the DBF field width; area_ha was kept.
msg_vetor_bloqueado: The previous vector file is in use in QGIS or locked by the system. Saving the new file as: {path}
msg_transitavel: Area walkable without exceptional effort (classes 1 and 2): {pct:.1f}% of the valid area.
msg_camada_pontos_abrir: Could not open the point layer: {path}
msg_ponto_sem_celula: The start or end point fell outside the viable cells, and there is no valid cell nearby.
msg_ponto_fora_mde: The {label} ({x}, {y}) lies outside the DEM extent (x {x0} to {x1}, y {y0} to {y1}, in the working CRS). Check the CRS of the points: typed coordinates are read in the project CRS.
msg_ponto_deslocado: The {label} fell in a non-viable cell and was moved {distance:,.0f} m to the nearest viable cell ({x}, {y} in the working CRS). Length, time and ascent refer to the moved path.
msg_sem_ligacao: The route points could not be connected: there is no path of viable cells between them.{hint}
msg_ligacao_declividade: With the maximum slope at {needed}% (now {current:g}%), the points connect. On a {cell:.0f} m DEM, the hiking trails tested fitted within 85%; above that there are usually sections with cables, chains or via ferrata: raise the limit only if the route is of that kind.
msg_ligacao_nem_sem_limite: Not even without a slope limit do the points connect: what separates them is a constraint in avoid mode, a watercourse above the fordable ceiling, NoData in the DEM, or the search margin.
msg_contato_vertice: The points connect only through a vertex contact: somewhere along the way, two impassable cells touch diagonally and the passage has zero width. What is missing here is width, not slope: increase the constraint buffer or use a higher-resolution DEM, in which the real passage is more than one cell wide.
msg_contato_vertice_trecho: The two points connect only through a vertex contact: somewhere along the way, two impassable cells touch diagonally and the passage has zero width. Up to version 1.2.0 the route escaped through such a vertex, describing a crossing that does not exist on the ground. What is missing here is width, not slope: reduce the minimum patch area so that walkable areas are not sliced, increase the constraint buffer, or use a higher-resolution DEM, in which the real passage is more than one cell wide.
msg_sem_caminho: The route points could not be connected: there is no path of viable cells between them. Common causes: a maximum slope too low for the relief (cells above it are impassable), a constraint layer in "{avoid}" mode surrounding one of the points, watercourses above the fordable ceiling separating the points, or a small lateral search margin. Raise the maximum slope, switch the constraint to "{penalise}", raise the largest fordable basin or widen the margin.
msg_desvio: The route goes around terrain above the maximum slope ({limit:g}%). Without the limit, it would be {free_km:.1f} km instead of {route_km:.1f} km, with {metres:.0f} m on slopes of up to {needed}%. Real trails often cross such terrain by cables, steps or switchbacks that a {cell:.0f} m DEM cannot resolve: if the route you want is of that kind, raise the maximum slope to {needed}%. If not, the detour is the way that avoids this terrain.
msg_area_busca_vazia: The route search area contains no viable cells.
msg_cancelado_rota: Route calculation cancelled by the user.
msg_cancelado_ordem: Order optimisation cancelled by the user.
msg_cancelado_drenagem: Drainage extraction cancelled by the user.
msg_rota_poucos_pontos: A route needs at least two points.
msg_mesma_celula_trecho: Points {a} and {b} fall in the same raster cell. Use points farther apart or a higher-resolution DEM.
msg_otimizacao_max: Order optimisation accepts up to {max} intermediate points; {n} were given. With more than that, give the order you want and turn optimisation off.
msg_otimizando: Optimising the order of {n} intermediate points ({legs} legs to compute).
msg_ordem_custos: given order: cost {given:.4f}; best order: cost {best:.4f} ({change:+.1f}%)
msg_folga_falhou: Could not create the slack raster.
msg_corredor_zero: The corridor width must be greater than zero.
msg_margem_zero: The route search margin must be greater than zero.
msg_area_busca_grande: The route search area became too large. Reduce the search margin or use closer points so that the calculation does not freeze.
msg_recorte: Access planning: clip of {cols:,} x {rows:,} cells; margin of {margin:.0f} m
msg_tobler_sem_mde: The walking-time model needs the DEM, which was not passed on.
msg_mesma_celula: The start and end points fall in the same raster cell. Use points farther apart or a higher-resolution raster to generate a route.
msg_rota_lago: The route crosses {n} cell(s) of flat water surface, a lake or reservoir flattened in the DEM. Tick "{option}" to treat them as a barrier.
msg_duracao: Estimated duration: {tobler:.2f} h at Tobler's pace ({max_speed:.1f} km/h maximum speed) and {field:.2f} h at field-survey pace ({field_speed:.1f} km/h, measured in a botanical inventory). The route is the same in both cases: the maximum speed changes the duration, not the path.
msg_travessia_aviso_campo: Estimated from relief only (contributing area). Depth and current vary with season and rain: check in the field before relying on it.
msg_travessias_resumo: The route crosses {crossings} watercourse(s) and runs along a watercourse in {along} stretch(es), totalling {km:.1f} km: {items}. Saved to {path}. Check in the field: the DEM knows neither flow nor season, and a stretch along a stream may flood in rain.
msg_sem_travessias: The route crosses no watercourse of the extracted network.
msg_tempo_tobler: Estimated walking time (Tobler, anisotropic): {hours:.2f} h ({hms}), mean speed {speed:.2f} km/h.
msg_alternativas_grande: Alternatives corridor not computed: the search area has {cells:,} cells, above the ceiling of {limit:,}. Reduce the search margin.
msg_alternativas_resumo: Alternatives corridor (up to {pct:g}% above the optimal cost): {area:,.1f} ha; the farthest alternative path passes {distance:,.0f} m from the route.
msg_alternativas_aviso: There are paths up to {pct:g}% costlier that pass {distance:,.0f} m from the route: the model does not pin it down well, and another clip of the DEM or another pixel size may swap it for one of those corridors. Read the alternatives corridor, not just the line.
msg_rota_nao_gerada: The route was not generated: {error} The zones and the maps are delivered anyway.
msg_concluido_sem_rota: Finished WITHOUT the route (the zones and the maps were generated): {error}
msg_transit_limites_texto: Could not read the transitability limits: {text}. Enter four increasing numbers separated by commas, in percent.
msg_transit_limites_quatro: The transitability limits must be exactly four increasing values, in percent. {n} were given.
msg_raster_sem_crs: The {name} raster has no CRS defined.
msg_gdal_camada: GDAL could not open the {name} layer: {source}
msg_pontos_obrigatorios: Provide both points, start and end. Both are required to generate the route.
msg_pesos_soma: The sum of the weights must be greater than zero.
msg_altitude_ordem: The minimum elevation must be lower than the maximum elevation.
msg_declividade_positiva: The slope limits must be greater than zero.
msg_area_minima_negativa: The minimum patch area cannot be negative (-1 = automatic).
msg_limiar_faixa_valida: The threshold must be between 0 and 1.
msg_percentil_faixa: The automatic percentile must be between 0 and 100.
msg_folga_faixa: The alternatives corridor slack must be between 0 and {max:.0f}%.
msg_corredor_margem: The corridor and the search margin must be greater than zero.
msg_param_decl_graus: Input slope raster in degrees (it will be converted to percent)
msg_param_area_auto: Minimum patch area: automatic (0.05% of the analysed area, 1 to 50 ha)
msg_param_zonas: Vector zones: {zones}; walkable mode: {walkable}; threshold by elevation band: {bands} ({size:.0f} m)
msg_camadas_obrigatorias: Without deriving from the DEM, the following layers are required: {layers}. Tick "{option}" or provide the rasters.
msg_rasters_fornecidos: Slope and curvature rasters were provided and will be used; derivation from the DEM was skipped.
msg_pes_metros: DEM converted from feet to metres: it now spans {min:,.0f} to {max:,.0f} m.
msg_pes_metros_curto: DEM converted from feet to metres.
msg_projecao_diferente: {name} has a different projection from the DEM.
msg_agua_retirada: Flattened water surface removed from the analysis: {sea:,.2f} km² of sea or NoData at 0 m{lakes}.
msg_agua_lagos: and {area:,.2f} km² of lakes and reservoirs
msg_cursos_classe: Watercourses by basin class (cells): {items}. Above {ford:.1f} km², fording is not assumed.
msg_faixa_altitude: The configured elevation range ({min:,.0f}–{max:,.0f} m) discards {pct:.1f}% of the area: {above:.1f}% above the maximum and {below:.1f}% below the minimum. The DEM spans {dem_min:,.0f} to {dem_max:,.0f} m. If the relief of this area falls outside that range, adjust the limits before interpreting the result.
msg_mascara_zonas: Zone mask: {viable:,} viable pixels out of {total:,} ({pct:.2f}%)
msg_mascara_rota: Route mask: {viable:,} navigable pixels out of {total:,} ({pct:.2f}%)
msg_extra_sem_raster: The additional criterion has a weight above zero, but no raster was given. Choose the layer or set the weight to zero.
msg_extra_sem_validos: The additional criterion raster has no valid cell over the DEM area. Check that it covers the study area.
msg_extra_constante: The additional criterion raster is practically constant over the study area (P05 = {low:.4g}, P95 = {high:.4g}); it distinguishes nothing.
msg_extra_resumo: Additional criterion: P05={low:.4g}, P95={high:.4g}, covers {coverage:.1f}% of the valid area, weight {weight:.2f}, {direction}.
msg_extra_cobertura: The additional criterion covers only {coverage:.1f}% of the study area. Uncovered cells are scored by the other criteria only, with the weights renormalised; compare them with care.
msg_twi_sem_drenagem: The terrain wetness weight requires the drainage extracted from the DEM. Tick "{option}" or set that weight to zero.
msg_sem_celulas_rota: No cell meets the route constraints. {cause}
msg_sem_celulas: No cell meets the configured constraints. {cause}
msg_causa_altitude: The configured elevation range ({min:,.0f} to {max:,.0f} m) does not cover the DEM, which spans {dem_min:,.0f} to {dem_max:,.0f} m: adjust the minimum and maximum elevation.
msg_causa_declividade: Only {pct:.1f}% of the terrain has slope up to the maximum allowed ({limit:g}%); the scene median is {median:.0f}%.
msg_causa_sem_celulas: The DEM has no valid cells.
msg_causa_geral: Check the elevation range, the maximum slope and the constraints.
msg_hidro_resolucao: Invalid spatial resolution for extracting the drainage.
msg_hidro_sem_celulas: The DEM has no valid cells for extracting the drainage.
msg_hidro_reamostrada: Hydrology computed on a grid resampled {factor}x ({cols:,} x {rows:,} cells, {pixel:.0f} m pixel) to keep the response time down.
msg_drenagem_resumo: Drainage extracted from the DEM: threshold of {threshold:.2f} km², {network:,.0f} km of network over {area:,.0f} km², density of {density:.2f} km/km².
msg_hidro_largura: The network was computed on a {pixel:.0f} m pixel, so each watercourse is at least that wide when mapped back to the DEM grid; a requested buffer smaller than that has no practical effect. For a narrower strip, clip the study area or provide a vector hydrography layer.
msg_hidro_celula_grossa: Drainage was extracted on a {pixel:.0f} m pixel. In the tests, a 90 m DEM found only about half of the mapped rivers (against 80% with a 30 m DEM). Check the watercourses against official hydrography before going to the field, or {remedy}.
msg_remedio_recorte: clip the study area so that drainage is computed at the DEM's resolution
msg_hidro_densidade: The resulting drainage density ({density:.2f} km/km²) is outside the usual range of 1 to 3 km/km² for mountainous relief. If the network looks too dense, raise the contributing-area threshold; if it looks too sparse, lower it.
msg_mde_grande_erro: The DEM has {cells:,} cells; deriving slope, curvatures and roughness would need about {gb:.1f} GB of transient memory and would very likely close QGIS. Clip the DEM to the area of interest (Raster > Extraction > Clip Raster by Extent) or resample to a larger cell before running.
msg_mde_grande: Large DEM: {cells:,} cells. Derivation may use about {gb:.1f} GB of memory and take several minutes. Clipping to the area of interest gives the same result with a shorter wait.
msg_resolucao_relevo: Invalid spatial resolution in the GeoTransform for deriving terrain.
msg_mde_pequeno: The DEM must have at least 2 x 2 cells to derive {what}; got {shape}.
msg_decl_derivada: Slope derived from the DEM ({px:.1f} x {py:.1f} m): p50={p50:.1f}%, p95={p95:.1f}%, max={max:.1f}%
msg_curvatura_derivada: {name} curvature derived from the DEM: p05={p05:.4g}, p50={p50:.4g}, p95={p95:.4g}
msg_tri: Roughness (TRI) derived from the DEM: p50={p50:.2f} m, p90={p90:.2f} m, max={max:.2f} m
msg_vrm: Vector ruggedness (VRM) derived from the DEM: p50={p50:.5f}, p90={p90:.5f}, max={max:.5f}
msg_transit_crescentes: The slope limits of the classes must be increasing.
msg_transit_celula_grossa: {cell:.0f} m cell: slope is smoothed by the resolution, and the classes come out systematically milder than the real terrain. On the same terrain, going from 30 m to 250 m moves 27 percentage points of the area into class 1. Report the cell size with any figure taken from this map.
msg_transit_vrm: Ruggedness (VRM, dimensionless) above {limit:.4f} (scene P{p:.0f}) moved {cells:,} cells down one class.
msg_transit_twi: Wetness above TWI {limit:.2f} (scene P{p:.0f}) moved {cells:,} cells down one class.
